treaty_name: Convention between the Portuguese Republic and the Republic of Bulgaria for the avoidance of double taxation and the prevention of fiscal evasion with respect to taxes on income (1995)
eif_quote: BULGÁRIA Resolução da Assembleia da República n.º 14/1996 ... Aviso n.º 258/96 publicado em 26-08-1996 EM VIGOR DESDE 18-07-1996
source_title: Diário da República I-A n.º 86, 11-4-1996 (Resolução AR 14/96): Convention PT-BG, Portuguese and English texts (Portal das Finanças)

rates.quote: Notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph 2, if the beneficial owner is a company that, for an uninterrupted period of two years prior to the payment of the dividend, owns directly at least 25 per cent of the capital stock (capital social) of the company paying the dividends, the tax so charged shall not exceed with respect to dividends paid after December 31, 1996, 10 per cent of the gross amount of such dividends.

However, such dividends may also be taxed in the Contracting State of which the company paying the dividends is a resident and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the dividends is a resident of the other Contracting State the tax so charged shall not exceed 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends.

However, such interest may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the interest is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the interest.

However, such royalties may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise, and according to the laws of that State, but if the recipient is the beneficial owner of the royalties the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.

ppt.quote: Pursuant to Article 35(6) of the Convention, the Portuguese Republic reserves the right for Article 35(4) not to apply with respect to its Covered Tax Agreements.

notes: Dividend 10% tier: company beneficial owner holding directly >=25% of capital for an uninterrupted two-year period before payment (modelled as 730 days). Portugal reserved MLI Art. 8 for this treaty under Art. 8(3)(b)(i) because it already contains a minimum holding period, so no MLI 365-day rule. Interest exempt at source (Art. 11(3)) for government debtors, government/institution financing under intergovernmental agreements, and central-bank / state-controlled financial institution loans as agreed - not modelled. Art. 28(2): WHT applies from 1 January of the year following EIF (EIF 1996-07-18 -> 1997-01-01). Protocol point 1: Bulgarian nationals resident in a third country do not get benefits on Portuguese-source income. MLI: covered by both (treaty map); PPT date 2023-01-01 = Art. 35(1)(a) after Bulgaria's MLI EIF 2023-01-01 (Bulgaria applies Art. 35(1), confirmed in the PL-BG synthesised text); no Portuguese or Bulgarian Art. 35(7) reservation found. The quoted PPT line is from Portugal's MLI position (no PT-BG synthesised text found). Authentic text English quoted from the Diário da República publication.
unverified: No PT-BG synthesised MLI text read; PPT date derived from Art. 35(1)(a) and treaty map
